title: CRLR/128/2024 of SUNIL KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.128 of 2024
Sunil Kumar .............Revisionist
Versus

Present:-
Mr. R.C. Tamta and Ms. Shobha Mehra, Advocates
for the revisionist.
Mr. M.A. Khan, AGA for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
order dated 22.01.2024, passed in Criminal Case No.315
of 2023, Pooja Devi vs. Sunil Kumar, passed by the court
of Judge, Family Court, Haldwani, District Nainital ("the
case").
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The case is based on an application filed under
Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the
Code") by the respondent no.2 seeking maintenance for
herself and her minor daughter respondent no.3.
According to the private respondents, respondent no.2
and the revisionist were married on 07.05.2017, but after

2
marriage the respondent no.2 was harassed and tortured
in connection with demand of dowry. The respondent no.3
was born from the wedlock on 25.03.2018. There were
compromise between the parties during the period, but
according to the respondent no.2, on 10.01.2020, the
revisionist expelled her from her matrimonial house with
her minor daughter. She has no means to maintain
herself whereas, the revisionist earns `70,000/- per
month. In the case an application for interim
maintenance was filed by the respondent no.2.
4. The revisionist did file objections to it. He
admits the marriage, but according to him, the
respondent no.2 was not giving respect to his family
members and she would not serve the meals properly.
The revisionist writes in his objections that he would
request the respondent no.2 to help his mother, but the
respondent no.2 never care for her mother-in-law.
According to the revisionist, he gets `30,000/- gross
salary. He has taken loan also. According to the
revisionist, the respondent no.2 is able to maintain
herself.

3
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that if efforts for mediation are made, perhaps the
parties may arrive at an amicable settlement.
6. On merits, learned counsel for the revisionist
would submit that the amount of maintenance provided
to the respondent no.3, the daughter of the parties @
`4,500/- may be maintained, but he would submit that
the amount of interim maintenance as fixed @ `5,000/-
per month to the respondent no.2 needs interference
because he did not have such means to pay that much
amount.
7. It is a revision against the order granting
interim maintenance. Much of the discussion at this stage
is not expected of unless there are some patent defects.
The chances of interference in this is much less.
Moreover, evidence may not be appreciated unless
irrelevant material is taken into considered or relevant
material is not considered or the finding is perverse.
8. Admittedly, the revisionist is the husband of
the respondent no.2 and respondent no.3 is their
daughter. The gross salary of the revisionist, according to
him, is `28,324/- and he gets `25,667/- as net salary.

4
9. Having considered the position of the parties in
society, their resources, etc. the court below fixed
`5,000/- an interim maintenance to the respondent no.2
and `4,500/- to the respondent no.3, the daughter of the
parties. This amount may not be termed to be excessive.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that there is no reason
to make any interference in this revision. Accordingly, the
revision deserves to be dismissed at the stage of
admission itself.
10. The revision is dismissed in limine.
11. The revisionist may very well move an
application before the court below seeking indulgence of
the court for mediation. This Court has no doubt that if,
such an application is moved, all efforts would be made
so that if possible, the parties may arrive at an amicable
settlement.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 22.02.2024
Sanjay
